The '''2022–23 Belgian Pro League''' (officially known as the '''Jupiler Pro League''' due to sponsorship reasons) was the 120th season of top-tier football in [[Belgium]]. [[Royal Antwerp F.C.|Royal Antwerp]] were crowned league champions for the first time in 66 years after pipping [[K.R.C. Genk|Genk]] and [[Royale Union Saint-Gilloise|Union St-Gilloise]] on the final day,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2023/jun/04/alderweireld-earns-royal-antwerp-first-belgian-league-title-in-66-years|title= Alderweireld earns Royal Antwerp first Belgian league title in 66 years|work=The Guardian|date = 5 June 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/watch-royal-antwerp-belgian-title-first-time-66-years-break-trophy/blt70173f77a3cd4839|title= Royal Antwerp lift Belgian league title for the first time in 66 years - and break the trophy during the celebrations!|publisher=Goal.com|date = 5 June 2023}}</ref> the first occasion since 1999 that three clubs were still contending the title going in the final match. All three Championship chasers were in the virtual lead in the table at different stages across the final five minutes before [[Toby Alderweireld]]'s title-clinching goal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/story/_/id/37799242/belgian-title-changes-hands-three-s-five-minutes-wont-find-wilder-end-season|title= Title changes hands 3 times in 5 minutes, Alderweireld stunner seals trophy: You won't find a wilder end to a season than in Belgium|publisher=[[ESPN]]|author=Chris Wright|date = 5 June 2023}}</ref> 

Genk's title-challenge was helped by a record-breaking 24 assists from [[Mike Trésor]] while [[Hugo Cuypers]] of [[K.A.A. Gent|Gent]] became the first Belgian winner of the Golden Bull for top scorer since [[Romelu Lukaku]] in 2009–10.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.voetbalnieuws.be/news/717534/cuypers-geeft-gouden-stier-extra-glans-cercle-dankt-oude-bekende|title=Cuypers geeft Gouden Stier extra glans, Cercle dankt oude bekende (Cuypers gives Golden Bull extra shine, Cercle thanks old acquaintance)|publisher=Voetbal Niewus|language=nl|date = 3 June 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nieuwsblad.be/cnt/dmf20230604_91955432|title=Buffalo's sluiten seizoen met een glimlach én de nodige vraagtekens af: "Komende weken zullen meer duidelijkheid brengen" (Buffalos end the season with a smile and the necessary question marks: "The coming weeks will bring more clarity")|publisher=Het Nieuwsblad|language=nl|date = 4 June 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://onefootball.com/id/berita/hugo-cuypers-becomes-first-belgian-top-scorer-in-the-pro-league-since-a-teenage-romelu-lukaku-37616605|title= Hugo Cuypers becomes first Belgian top scorer in the Pro League since a teenage Romelu Lukaku|publisher=OneFootball|date = 5 June 2023}}</ref>

[[S.V. Zulte Waregem|Zulte Waregem]], pipped for the title on the final day ten years earlier and subsequent Cup winners in 2017, were one of three sides relegated.

==Format change==
At the end of the [[2019–20 Belgian First Division A]], it was decided to exceptionally cancel any relegations as a result of the league being stopped early due to the COVID-19 pandemic. This caused the league to temporarily expand to 18 as promotions from a lower league did occur as originally planned. It was decided at that point that the goal was to eventually return to 16 teams, and at the end of the [[2021–22 Belgian First Division A]], the clubs agreed that the 2022–23 season will reduce the number of clubs at the highest level again to 16, as this season only three teams will face direct relegation instead of just one. Furthermore, a new format was also decided from 2023–24 onwards (with 16 teams), returning to a slightly altered version of the playoff structure used prior to the 2019–20 season, but most importantly also increasing the teams relegating each season from 1 to 2 direct plus an additional optional third team through a playoff.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sporza.be/nl/2022/06/17/witte-rook-over-nieuwe-competitieformule-in-1a-16-ploegen-tot-3-dalers-halvering-blijft~1655456366658/|language=dutch|title = Witte rook over nieuwe competitieformule in 1A: 16 ploegen, tot 3 dalers, halvering blijft|trans-title = White smoke on new competition format in 1A: 16 teams, up to 3 teams facing relegation, halving of points remains|date = 17 June 2022}}</ref> A minor change was the renaming of the top two leagues, with the First Division A and First Division B now renamed Jupiler Pro League and Challenger Pro League respectively.

==Teams==
Eighteen teams competed in the league – the top seventeen teams from the previous season and [[2021–22 Belgian First Division B]] champions [[K.V.C. Westerlo|Westerlo]] who returned after spending five seasons at the second tier following their relegation at the end of the [[2016–17 Belgian First Division A|2016–17 season]]. They replaced [[K Beerschot VA|Beerschot]] who had finished last by a very large margin and were relegated after two seasons at the highest level. No other changes happened as [[R.F.C. Seraing (1922)|Seraing]] (who finished 17th) won the [[2021–22 Belgian First Division A#Promotion-Relegation play-off|Relegation play-off]] against [[RWDM47|RWDM]], and thus stayed in the top division.

==Relegations==
With three clubs being relegated, there was a major turnover in coaches with most clubs changing coach during the season. Out of the 18 Pro League sides, only seven kept the same coach from the opening day to the last. [[R.F.C. Seraing (1922)|Seraing]] became the first club to be relegated, following a 2–0 away loss to [[Club Brugge KV|Club Brugge]] on 7 April 2023. One week later, on 15 April 2023, [[K.V. Oostende|Oostende]] also dropped as they went down 0–4 at home to [[Oud-Heverlee Leuven|OH Leuven]]. Yet another week later, on the final matchday of the regular season, [[S.V. Zulte Waregem|Zulte Waregem]] became the third and final team relegated following a 2–3 home loss to [[Cercle Brugge K.S.V.|Cercle Brugge]].

==Play-offs==

===Play-off I===
Points obtained during the regular season were halved (and rounded up in the event of half-points) before the start of the playoff. Genk and Union SG, therefore, started on 38 points, Antwerp on 36, and Club Brugge on 30. Only Antwerp did not see their points rounded up, hence in case of ties they were always ranked above the other teams. Any other ties were broken by regular season finishing order (Genk, then Union SG, then Club Brugge).

===Play-off II===
Points obtained during the regular season will be halved (and rounded up) before the start of the playoff. Gent and Standard started on 28 points, Westerlo on 26, and Cercle Brugge on 25. As the points of Standard and Westerlo were rounded up, in case of ties they would always be ranked below the team (or teams) they are tied with. The deciding factor after that would be finishing position in the regular season.
